reception.text: The proclamation drew little notice; because Congress had authorized it by name, it set off none of the lock-up arguments that met the forest reserves.

political_impact.text: Hunting, trapping, killing or capturing game on federal land north and west of the Colorado River became unlawful except under the Secretary of Agriculture's regulations.
Grazing continued on the plateau, and cattle there rose from about 9,000 head in 1906 to more than 15,000 by 1913.
Government hunters trapped or shot 781 mountain lions, 30 wolves, 4,889 coyotes and 554 bobcats on the plateau between 1906 and 1931.
Cattle and sheep operators on the plateau spent years contesting how much forage the growing deer herd left for livestock.

legacy.text: From 1906 to 1939, 816 mountain lions, 30 wolves, 7,388 coyotes and 863 bobcats were removed from the plateau.
The Kaibab deer irruption and crash became a standard textbook example of what happens when predators are removed, and Aldo Leopold named the pattern the "Kaibab-Sequence."
legacy.source: Leopold, Sowls and Spencer, Journal of Wildlife Management 11 (1947)

legacy.text: Graeme Caughley showed the herd estimates were badly inconsistent, with 1924 figures ranging from 30,000 to 100,000.

Binkley and colleagues found converging evidence, including aspen age structure, for a real deer irruption in the late 1910s and 1920s shaped by drought, grazing and fire suppression as well as predator removal.
The preserve was never abolished; its provisions survive at 16 U.S.C. §§ 683–687 and the Forest Service still administers it.

today.name: Grand Canyon Game Preserve
today.note: A designated area of the Kaibab National Forest, closed to locatable mineral entry.
today.source: Kaibab National Forest Land and Resource Management Plan (2014)

today.name: Kaibab National Forest, North Kaibab Ranger District
Grand Canyon National Park
today.note: The park took part of the preserve in 1919 and covers the plateau's southern end.

related.note: Added ground south of the canyon, with a diagram.
The Wichita game preserve rested on a 1905 act that the 1906 Grand Canyon act copied almost word for word.

later_actions.text: Proclamation 875 diminished the preserve, leaving it at 1,492,928 acres.
Congress carved Grand Canyon National Park partly out of the preserve.
President Hoover's Proclamation 1971 diminished the preserve again.
Reorganization Plan No. II moved the Wichita preserve to Interior but left the Grand Canyon preserve with Agriculture.
The Kaibab forest plan lists the preserve as a designated area with the desired condition that it provides quality habitat for game animals.
later_actions.source: Kaibab NF Land and Resource Management Plan (2014)

uncertain: The preserve's size at creation is not known; the proclamation gives no acreage and the 1906 Yearbook figure of 2,267,300 acres cannot be right.
